newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil sold down on crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil sold down on crude.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil swaps traded down late afternoon on weaker overnight crude prices and poor demand from China, traders said on Tuesday.
"The fuel oil market was sold down this afternoon as people expected the physical market to came off sharply in line with the weaker crude," one trader said.
March swaps were last quoted at $97.00/$98.00 per tonne, down sharply from Friday's $99.50/$100.50.
The market traded earlier in the day at $97.50 per tonne compared to a traded low of $99.50 last night, brokers said.
April swaps was also down and was last quoted at $96.00/$97.50 per tonne from Friday's $99.00/$99.75. It traded earlier in the day at $99.50 per tonne, brokers said.
Traders said the fall in fuel oil swaps were in line with the crude fall and the emergence of physical selling interest on Monday.
A major offered 20,000-tonnes of 180-cst high suplur fuel oil at $101.50 per tonne free-on-board Singapore, down $2.00 per tonne from Thursday's offered price, but no buyers emerged.
Traders said there are strong expectations of further physical offers late in the day for physical cargoes at lower levels.
March gas oil swaps were last quoted at $24.55/$24.65 per barrel, down from Monday's $25.00/$25.10, brokers said.
The market opened to trade at $24.60 per barrel and was later traded up at $24.65 and $24.75, but retreated slightly in the afternoon, to trade at $24.65, brokers said.

Weaker prices were partly attributed to a hefty 67 cents loss to April Brent crude on the International Petroleum Exchange to $19.12 per barrel and a $3.75 per tonne loss to March gas oil futures closing at $166.75 on Monday.
Traders said lower gas oil purchases by India for April arrival at 570,000-tonnes compared to the original expectation of 700,000 also dampened market sentiment.
India's additional tender to buy 270,000-tonnes was discounted by some quarters who felt that India may not take the full volume.
